([[Hollywood, Florida]]) | college = *[[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia]] (2019–2021) *[[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]] (2021–2023) | draft_year = 2023 | draft_round = 2 | draft_pick = 52 | draft_team = [[Phoenix Suns]] | career_start = 2023 | years1 = {{nbay|2023|start}}–present | team1 = [[Portland Trail Blazers]] | highlights = *[[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] ({{nbay|2024|end}}) *First-team All-[[Atlantic 10]] (2023) *Third-team All-Atlantic 10 (2022) *Atlantic 10 All-Defensive team (2023) }} '''Toumani Camara''' ({{IPAc-en|t|uː|ˈ|m|ɑː|n|i|_|k|ə|ˈ|m|ɑːr|ə}} {{respelling|too|MAH|nee|_|kə|MAR|ə}};{{cite press release |author= |title=2023-24 start of season NBA pronunciation guide |url=https://www.nba.com/news/2023-24-start-of-season-nba-pronunciation-guide |publisher=National Basketball Association |date=October 24, 2023 |access-date=May 18, 2024}} born 8 May 2000) is a Belgian professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Portland Trail Blazers|Portland Trail Blazers]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). Raised in Belgium, he moved to the United States to attend [[Chaminade–Madonna College Preparatory School]] in [[Hollywood, Florida]]. Camara started his [[college basketball]] career with the [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Georgia Bulldogs]] and then transferred to the [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]] after his sophomore season. He was selected in the [[2023 NBA draft]] by the [[Phoenix Suns]] and traded to the Trail Blazers before the start of his rookie season. ==Early life== Camara was raised in [[Brussels]], Belgium.{{cite web |last=Archdeacon |first=Tom |date=26 October 2021 |title=Archdeacon: Transfer gets second chance to make impression at UD |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/archdeacon-transfer-gets-second-chance-to-make-impression-at-ud/GFSUJGXQY5BTHG2HBLUXRLHCFQ/ |access-date=26 May 2023 |website=Dayton Daily News}} His mother, Anne Le Docte, is of Belgian and [[Haitians|Haitian]] origin while his father is from Mali. Camara and his older brother were raised solely by Le Docte since he was five years old.{{cite web |last=Archdeacon |first=Tom |title=Archdeacon: UD Arena sendoff for Camara is well-deserved |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/archdeacon-ud-arena-sendoff-for-camara-is-well-deserved/LOE7IO2CIZHSZFZRWIQMURX764/ |website=Dayton Daily News |access-date=26 May 2023 |date=2 March 2023}} He had a sister who died from a lung ailment when she was three months old. Camara has four butterflies tattooed on his right leg to pay tribute to his family: his mother, his brother, his sister and himself. Camara first started playing basketball after being influenced by his brother. A local basketball court was occupied by [[soccer]] players throughout the day and Camara would have to wait until nighttime to play. His first exposure to American basketball was the [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament]] which was broadcast on Belgian television. Camara stayed awake into early mornings when he found a website that broadcast live [[NBA]] games and became a fan of [[Dwyane Wade]] while he watched him win a championship with the [[Miami Heat]]. Camara developed into a promising player and played for the [[Belgium men's national under-16 basketball team|Belgium national team]] that competed in the [[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship Division B]]. His Belgian coach had a friend who coached in [[Weston, Florida]], and agreed to help Camara find a school in the United States. Camara moved to the United States at the age of 16 to attend [[Chaminade-Madonna College Preparatory School]] in [[Hollywood, Florida]]. ==High school career== Camara played at Chaminade-Madonna College Preparatory School where he averaged a [[double-double]] in his junior and senior seasons. He was recruited by more than 30 [[NCAA Division I]] schools. Camara toured the [[University of Dayton]] and [[Kansas State University]] but committed to the [[University of Georgia]] to play for the [[Georgia Bulldogs basketball|Bulldogs]] on 1 October 2018. ==College career== Camara averaged 6.6 points and 4.3 rebounds per game during his freshman season with the Bulldogs.{{cite web |title=Georgia’s Toumani Camara earns SEC honor |url=https://www.ajc.com/sports/georgia-bulldogs/georgias-toumani-camara-earns-sec-honor/XKLWK4M4VZHLBNCRL6JTLQQMOQ/ |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=26 May 2023 |date=22 December 2020}} During his [[2019–20 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|freshman season]], he was teammates with future #1 pick of the [[2020 NBA draft]], [[Anthony Edwards (basketball)|Anthony Edwards]]. He was mentioned as a possible NBA prospect before the start of his sophomore season but his stock fell.{{cite web |last=Weiszer |first=Marc |title=UGA basketball takes a hit with forward Toumani Camara latest in transfer portal |url=https://www.onlineathens.com/story/sports/college/bulldogs-extra/2021/04/01/uga-basketball-takes-big-hit-toumani-camara-transfer-portal/7019534002/ |website=Athens Banner-Herald |access-date=26 May 2023 |date=2 April 2021}} Camara finished his [[2020–21 Georgia Bulldogs basketball team|sophomore season]] with averages of 12.8 points and a team-best 7.7 rebounds per game. On 1 April 2021, Camara announced that he was entering the [[transfer portal]]; he stated that he felt like he would be able to develop more while playing for a different team. On 8 April 2021, Camara committed to play for [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton Flyers]].{{cite web |last=Jablonski |first=David |title=Georgia transfer commits to Dayton Flyers |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/georgia-transfer-commits-to-dayton-flyers/RPP2INLSSNF7RP5ODELM6WB3RM/ |website=Dayton Daily News |access-date=26 May 2023 |date=9 April 2021}} He averaged 10.9 points and 6.9 rebounds during the [[2021–22 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|2021–22 season]],{{cite web |last=Boyle |first=John |title=NBA Draft: Dayton sophomore on early-entry list |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/nba-draft-dayton-sophomore-on-early-entry-list/ELG54AXSVFC7PNPJW6VJI6PIGY/ |website=Dayton Daily News |access-date=26 May 2023 |date=27 April 2022}} earning him a nomination to the All-[[Atlantic 10 Conference]] third team.{{cite web |title=Brajkovic Named Atlantic 10 Player of the Year, McKillop, Osunniyi Earn Top Honors |url=https://atlantic10.com/news/2022/3/8/mens-basketball-brajkovic-named-atlantic-10-player-of-the-year-mckillop-osunniyi-earn-top-honors.aspx |website=Atlantic 10 Conference |access-date=26 May 2023 |date=8 March 2022}} Camara declared for the [[2022 NBA draft]] but withdrew after testing the process.{{cite web |last=Jablonski |first=David |title=Dayton forward withdraws name from NBA Draft |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/dayton-forward-withdraws-name-from-nba-draft/FT6B3WQABZAMBI5HMWEGJ5DLII/ |website=Dayton Daily News |access-date=26 May 2023 |date=21 May 2022}} He was appointed as the Flyers' team captain for the [[2022–23 Dayton Flyers men's basketball team|2022–23 season]] and was the only fourth-year player on the roster.{{cite web |last=Jablonski |first=David |title=Camara on 2 seasons at Dayton: ‘It’s been an amazing experience’ |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/camara-on-two-seasons-at-dayton-its-been-an-amazing-experience/DVJNFFWN55AFBJ2YVDF742HODY/ |website=Dayton Daily News |access-date=26 May 2023 |date=1 March 2023}} Camara averaged 13.9 points and 8.6 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last=Jablonski |first=David |title=Dayton’s Camara thanks Flyer Nation ‘for two amazing years’ |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/daytons-camara-thanks-flyer-nation-for-two-amazing-years/5NH4MEB5BFAYLFWROJGJXLQPVQ/ |website=Dayton Daily News |access-date=26 May 2023 |date=25 April 2023}} He was selected to the All-Atlantic 10 first team and the all-defensive team. On 25 April 2023, Camara announced that he had declared for the [[2023 NBA draft]] to forgo his final season of collegiate eligibility. He was invited to participate at the [[NBA Draft Combine]].{{cite web |last=Jablonski |first=David |title=Two Dayton forwards receive invitations to NBA Draft Combine |url=https://www.daytondailynews.com/sports/two-dayton-forwards-receive-invitations-to-nba-draft-combine/QP6KLJ3265C4HABEHSFRKTNOBU/ |website=Dayton Daily News |access-date=26 May 2023 |date=3 May 2023}} ==Professional career== ===Portland Trail Blazers (2023–present)=== Camara was drafted by the [[Phoenix Suns]] as the 52nd pick of the [[2023 NBA draft]].{{cite web|title=SUNS SELECT TOUMANI CAMARA WITH 52ND OVERALL PICK IN 2023 NBA DRAFT|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/news/suns-select-toumani-camara-with-52nd-overall-pick-in-2023-nba-draft|website=NBA.com|date=22 June 2023|access-date=27 September 2023}} Camara signed a four-year rookie scaled contract on 3 July 2023.{{cite tweet|author=Suns|title=That first NBA contract ✍️|number=1676033157139943425|user=Suns|date=3 July 2023|access-date=3 July 2023}} ====2023–24 season==== On 27 September 2023, Camara, alongside [[Jrue Holiday]], [[Deandre Ayton]] and a 2029 first-round draft pick, was traded to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] as part of a three-team deal that sent [[Damian Lillard]] to the [[Milwaukee Bucks]] and [[Grayson Allen]], [[Jusuf Nurkić]], [[Nassir Little]] and [[Keon Johnson (basketball, born 2002)|Keon Johnson]] to the Phoenix Suns.{{cite web |date=27 September 2023 |title=Trail Blazers Acquire Deandre Ayton, Jrue Holiday and Toumani Camara in Three Team Trade With Milwaukee Bucks and Phoenix Suns |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-acquire-deandre-ayton-jrue-holiday-and-toumani-camara-in-three-team-trade-with-milwaukee-bucks-and-phoenix-suns |access-date=27 September 2023 |website=NBA.com}} He made his Blazers debut on 25 October in a game against the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] where he recorded seven points, one assist and two rebounds.{{cite web |title=LIVE NBA. Toumani Camara krijgt 16 minuten in debuutmatch, Clippers maatje te groot voor Trail Blazers |url=https://www.hln.be/nba/live-nba-toumani-camara-krijgt-16-minuten-in-debuutmatch-clippers-maatje-te-groot-voor-trail-blazers~a4fde4c2/ |website=HLN |access-date=26 October 2023 |language=nl |date=26 October 2023}} Camara suffered a fractured left rib and a small laceration in his kidney at the end of March 2024 to end his rookie season early.{{cite web |title=Trail Blazers' Toumani Camara: Cleared for camp |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/trail-blazers-toumani-camara-cleared-for-camp/ |website=CBSSports.com |access-date=30 September 2024 |language=en |date=30 September 2024}} He averaged 7.5 points and 4.9 rebounds per game. ====2024–25 season==== On 30 September 2024, Camara was cleared for training camp. From 19 January to 6 February 2025, the Trail Blazers had won 10 of their last 11 games (the team improved to 23–29 after starting the season 13–28). Camara had been a huge part of the turnaround with his defensive intensity and improved second-year shooting. He averaged 11.8 PPG, 7.9 RPG, and 2.1 APG on 54.9% shooting and 46.9% from three-point range (and an average +/- of +13.9 per game) during the run.{{cite web |title=Inside Portland’s defensive resurgence |url=https://www.nba.com/news/inside-portlands-defensive-resurgence |website=NBA.com |date=5 February 2025 |access-date=5 March 2025 }} For his defensive play in February, he was named Western Conference Defensive Player of the Month.{{cite web |title=Toumani Camara Named Western Conference Defensive Player of the Month |url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/toumani-camara-named-western-conference-defensive-player-of-the-month |website=NBA.com |date=4 March 2025 |access-date=5 March 2025 }} Camara started all 78 games he played in for Portland during the [[2024–25 NBA season]], averaging 11.3 points, 5.8 rebounds, and 2.2 assists. At season's end, Camara became the first Trail Blazer since [[Theo Ratliff]] in 2004 to earn [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] honors when he was named to the All Defensive Second Team.{{Cite web |title=Toumani Camara Selected to NBA All-Defensive Second Team {{!}} Portland Trail Blazers |url=https://blazers.com/news/toumani-camara-selected-to-nba-all-defensive-second-team |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=blazers.com |language=en}} ====2025–26 season==== On October 19, 2025, Camara and the Trail Blazers agreed to a four-year, $82 million contract extension.{{cite web |last=Charania |first=Shams |author-link=Shams Charania |date=2025-10-19 |title=Agents: Blazers' Sharpe, Camara reach extensions |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/46652523/trail-blazers-toumani-camara-reach-4-year-extension-agent-says |access-date=2025-12-07 |website=ESPN.com}} On March 23, 2026, Camara hit a career–high nine three–point field goals on 11 attempts in a win against the [[2025–26 Brooklyn Nets season|Brooklyn Nets]].{{Cite web |title=Nets vs Trail Blazers, March 23, 2026 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/202603230POR.html |access-date=2026-05-03 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} Camara started all 82 contests for Portland during the [[2025–26 NBA season|2025–26 season]], recording averages of 13.4 points, 5.1 rebounds, and 2.5 assists.{{Cite web|title=Here Are The NBA's 2026-26 Iron Men. How Do They Compare To Years Past?|url=https://www.si.com/nba/iron-men-players-all-82-games-list-compared-years-past|access-date=July 31, 2026|website=si.com|language=en}} ==National team career== Camara was selected to represent Belgium on the youth level, at the [[2016 FIBA U16 European Championship Division B]]. During the tournament with the [[Belgium men's national under-16 basketball team|Belgium U16 national team]], he finished with averages of 2.4 points and 2.9 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=Toumani Camara 2016 FIBA U16 European Championship B profile |url=https://www.fiba.basketball/en/history/233-fiba-u16-eurobasket-division-b/9804/players/227067-toumani-camara |access-date=20
